# Tissametteyya Sutta (Snp 4.7 (PTS Snp 160))
**ID:** Snp 4.7 (PTS Snp 160)
**Section:** Suttanipāta (snp)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Tissametteyya Sutta
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/snp4.7
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0505m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Tissametteyya Sutta* is the seventh discourse in the *Aṭṭhakavagga* of the *Suttanipāta* (Snp 4.7, verses 814–823; PTS Snp 160) [Norman 1983; Norman 1997–2001; Anderson and Smith 1913]. The text is structured as a dialogue in verse between the Buddha and the venerable Tissa Metteyya, an interlocutor who should be distinguished from the youth of the same name appearing in the *Pārāyanavagga* (Snp 5.2) [Norman 1997–2001; Anderson and Smith 1913]. In the discourse, Tissametteyya asks the Buddha to explain the drawbacks and perils encountered by someone who indulges in sexual intercourse (*methuna*) [Saddhatissa 2013; Anderson and Smith 1913]. In response, the Buddha warns against sensual pleasures and falling away from celibacy, explaining that a practitioner devoted to sexual indulgence loses both spiritual practice and the Teaching, and urges the mendicant to train in seclusion, cross the stream, and wander free from sensual craving [SuttaCentral; Norman 1983; Saddhatissa 2013; Müller 1881]. According to the commentary (*Paramatthajotikā* II 589), Tissametteyya attained arahantship [Anālayo 2011].
Within the Pali Canon, the entire sutta is analyzed word by word in the *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 7, *Tissametteyyasuttaniddesa*), which DharmaNexus identifies as sharing 38 textual matches spanning its verses [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. The sutta is also referenced in the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 1) [SuttaCentral]. Outside the Pali tradition, a curated parallel exists in the Chinese translation of the *Arthapada Sūtra* (*Foshuo yizu jing*, T 198) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus also records several low-scoring text-reuse alignments with the Tibetan *Udānavarga* (D 4099) [DharmaNexus].
